Chapter 11. The Challenge of Modernity: Faith in a Changing World.
The world never stands still, does it? New ideas pop up every day. Technology keeps pushing us forward, and the ways we live are always shifting. Sure, that's exciting—sometimes it feels like anything is possible. But let’s be honest, all that change can throw us off balance. It's easy to wonder if the old faith still fits in a world that's racing toward the next big thing.
Picture a group of friends, each dealing with their own doubts and struggles. They started asking themselves—do those old stories still matter? Is faith just a leftover from another time, something we’ve outgrown? But as they talked, something clicked. Those big questions—about meaning, purpose, love—they haven’t changed at all.
The old faith, with all its mysteries and even its contradictions, offers more than just nostalgia. It’s a way of living that holds up, no matter how much the world changes. It reminds us that truth isn’t just whatever’s popular right now—it’s something real, something that lasts. The old faith invites us to look at the world with wonder, to accept both the hard parts and the joys of modern life.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we need that kind of steady ground. With so much uncertainty swirling around, it can be tough to know what to trust or where to plant our feet. The old faith gives us a foundation—a way to welcome change without losing our sense of who we are.
And here’s the thing: Faith isn’t about running away from the world. It’s about stepping into it, with courage and hope. The old faith invites us to bring our questions and our doubts. It dares us to wrestle with the challenges right in front of us and helps us find meaning even as everything else shifts.
